description: The three content-addressed primitives — atoms, bonds and molecules — and the fillers a molecule is built from. Every case gives the structure, its canonical dCBOR bytes, the 32-byte digest those bytes hash to, and the 36-byte CID with its canonical base32 text form.

sections.name: atoms
sections.description: atom = { "description" => tstr }. The digest of an atom is SHA-256 over these bytes and nothing else, so two atoms whose descriptions differ by one code point are two entities.

cases.name: france
cases.note: The worked example of spec/03-encoding.md, "Encoding an atom": every step of it, from the CBOR bytes to the base32 text form, is checked by this case.

cases.name: paris_the_capital_of_france
cases.note: The atom example of spec/01-data-model.md. Its description is 28 bytes, so the text string takes a one-byte length argument (78 1c).

cases.name: paris_france
cases.note: A second name for the same city, and a different entity. The two are related with the "_A_ is the same as _B_" meta-bond, never merged by an implementation.

cases.name: eiffel_tower
cases.note: Subject of the scalar molecule below.

cases.name: metre
cases.note: A unit atom. A scalar filler's optional unit field carries this digest, and that digest is subject to the same reachability rule as any other (spec/02-block-format.md, rule 4).

sections.name: bonds
sections.description: bond = { "template" => tstr }. The variables are the _X_ placeholders of the template, in the order they appear; a molecule's fillers are matched to them positionally.

cases.name: capital_of
cases.note: The bond example of spec/01-data-model.md.

cases.name: height
cases.note: A two-variable bond whose second filler is a scalar with a unit.

sections.name: meta_bonds
sections.description: The five standard meta-bonds of spec/06-meta-bonds.md. The specification prints their templates and no digests; these are the identifiers by which every implementation recognizes a meta-molecule, so they are pinned here.

cases.name: equivalence
cases.note: Transitive equivalence between two entities of the same kind (spec/06-meta-bonds.md §1).

cases.name: truth_assertion
cases.note: Asserts a molecule (§2).

cases.name: truth_retraction
cases.note: Retracts or denies a molecule (§3).

cases.name: contradiction
cases.note: Declares two molecules contradictory (§4).

cases.name: supersession
cases.note: Versioning: molecule A replaces molecule B (§5).

sections.name: molecules
sections.description: molecule = { "bond" => bstr .size 32, "fillers" => [+ filler] }. The bond is referenced by its raw digest, never by a CID.

cases.name: paris_is_the_capital_of_france
cases.note: The molecule example of spec/01-data-model.md: "[Paris, the capital of France] is the capital of [France]". Two atom fillers, positionally matched to _A_ and _B_.

cases.name: eiffel_tower_is_330_metres_tall
cases.note: A molecule whose second filler is a scalar carrying a unit digest: "[The Eiffel Tower] is [330 metre] tall".

cases.name: paris_equivalence
cases.note: A meta-molecule: the two Paris atoms are declared the same (spec/06-meta-bonds.md, "Declaring atom equivalence"). A meta-molecule is an ordinary molecule; only its bond digest marks it.

cases.name: truth_of_an_atom
cases.note: "_A_ is true" filled with an atom, where the meta-bond declares a molecule. It is a valid molecule and MUST be accepted: a meta-bond's Fillers line is a recognition criterion applied at L2→L3, not a validity rule (spec/06-meta-bonds.md, "Meta-molecules are regular molecules"). L3 reads no truth assertion from it and surfaces it as a plain molecule.

sections.name: fillers
sections.description: One case per filler type, including every scalar shape: a plain integer, a negative integer, a decimal fraction, a number with a unit, and a datetime range. A filler carries no identifier of its own.

cases.name: atom_reference
cases.note: Type 0: the raw 32-byte digest of an atom.

cases.name: bond_reference
cases.note: Type 1: the digest of a bond.

cases.name: molecule_reference
cases.note: Type 2: the digest of a molecule. This is how a meta-molecule names the molecule it asserts.

cases.name: ipfs_uri
cases.note: Type 3: an IPFS content identifier as text. It is not an internal reference; its format is IPFS's, not Dialog's.

cases.name: scalar_integer
cases.note: A unitless whole number. Whole numbers are plain CBOR integers, never decimal fractions.

cases.name: scalar_negative_integer
cases.note: A negative whole number, major type 1.

cases.name: scalar_decimal_fraction
cases.note: 3.14 as tag 4 [-2, 314] (spec/03-encoding.md, "Decimal fractions").

cases.name: scalar_with_unit
cases.note: 330 metres. The unit field carries the digest of the atom naming the unit, and that atom MUST be reachable from the block (spec/02-block-format.md, rule 4).

cases.name: scalar_decimal_with_unit
cases.note: 3.14 metres: a decimal fraction and a unit together. The map keys sort unit before value.

cases.name: scalar_datetime_range
cases.note: A datetime range. Both endpoints are UTC RFC 3339 date-times at second precision, and a range never carries a unit.

cases.name: scalar_datetime_instant
cases.note: A range whose endpoints are equal — the protocol's way of writing a single instant.

cases.name: scalar_datetime_leap_day
cases.note: 29 February 1600, a whole day. The calendar is the proleptic Gregorian one (spec/01-data-model.md, "Datetime ranges" rule 6), so this date exists although the Julian calendar in civil use in 1600 numbered its days differently; the invalid section's timestamp_julian_leap_day is the other half of the pair the specification works out.

sections.name: invalid
sections.description: Encodings the data model refuses. Every case is well-formed dCBOR — except where it says otherwise — that spec/01-data-model.md rejects, so a decoder that accepts one has entities its peers cannot read. The "kind" field names the decoder the bytes are handed to (atom, bond, molecule or filler); each case must be rejected by that decoder.

cases.name: atom_empty_description
cases.reason: An atom whose description is the empty string. "The description MUST be a non-empty UTF-8 string".

cases.name: atom_description_not_text
cases.reason: An atom whose description is the integer 1. The CDDL binds it to tstr.

cases.name: atom_unknown_key
cases.reason: An atom map carrying a "lang" key its definition does not declare. An unknown key is a rejection, never something to ignore: the digest is taken over these bytes.

cases.name: atom_missing_description
cases.reason: The empty map: the one key an atom's definition requires is absent.

cases.name: bond_empty_template
cases.reason: A bond whose template is the empty string.

cases.name: bond_template_without_a_variable
cases.reason: "is the capital of" declares no variable, and "The template MUST be a non-empty UTF-8 string containing one or more variables".

cases.name: bond_template_lowercase_variables
cases.reason: "_a_ is the same as _b_" looks like a two-variable template and is not one: UCALPHA is %x41-5A, so lowercase letters match no variable and this template declares none.

cases.name: bond_template_repeats_a_variable
cases.reason: "_A_ is the capital of _A_" uses the name A twice. "Variable names MUST be unique within a bond template", since fillers are matched to variables positionally.

cases.name: molecule_missing_fillers
cases.reason: A molecule map with a bond and no fillers key.

cases.name: molecule_unknown_key
cases.reason: A molecule map carrying a "ts" key. A molecule states a relationship and records no time; the block does that.

cases.name: molecule_empty_fillers
cases.reason: An empty fillers array. The CDDL says [+ filler]: one or more.

cases.name: molecule_bond_is_a_cid
cases.reason: The bond field carries the 36-byte CIDv1 of the bond instead of its raw 32-byte digest. Inside a Dialog structure every reference is a digest.

cases.name: filler_type_out_of_range
cases.reason: A filler of type 5. The v1 vocabulary is types 0 to 4, and "implementations MUST reject any type tag other than 0 to 4".

cases.name: filler_type_not_an_integer
cases.reason: A filler whose type tag is the text string "0".

cases.name: filler_reference_wrong_size
cases.reason: A type 0 filler whose value is 31 bytes. Types 0, 1 and 2 carry bstr .size 32.

cases.name: filler_reference_is_a_cid
cases.reason: A type 1 filler carrying a 36-byte CIDv1. The CID appears at the API boundary, never inside an entity.

cases.name: filler_reference_is_text
cases.reason: A type 2 filler whose value is a text string. The tag names the value shape, and molecule references are byte strings.

cases.name: filler_ipfs_uri_empty
cases.reason: A type 3 filler carrying the empty string. "An empty content identifier addresses nothing, and implementations MUST reject it."

cases.name: filler_ipfs_uri_is_bytes
cases.reason: A type 3 filler carrying a byte string. An IPFS URI is tstr — type 3 is not an internal reference.

cases.name: filler_scalar_is_an_integer
cases.reason: A type 4 filler whose value is the bare integer 330. A scalar filler's value is the scalar-value map, even for a unitless number.

cases.name: filler_unknown_key
cases.reason: A filler map carrying a "unit" key. The unit belongs inside a scalar filler's value, and a filler map declares exactly type and value.

cases.name: filler_missing_value
cases.reason: A filler map with a type and no value.

cases.name: scalar_unit_without_value
cases.reason: A scalar value carrying a unit and no value. The unit is optional in the CDDL; the value is not.

cases.name: scalar_unit_wrong_size
cases.reason: A scalar whose unit is 31 bytes. A unit is the SHA-256 digest of the atom naming it: bstr .size 32.

cases.name: scalar_value_is_text
cases.reason: A scalar whose value is the text string "330". A scalar is an integer or a tag 4 decimal fraction.

cases.name: scalar_unknown_key
cases.reason: A scalar value carrying a "scale" key its definition does not declare.

cases.name: scalar_non_canonical_decimal
cases.reason: A scalar carrying #6.4([0, 314]). The exponent MUST be negative — a whole number is a plain integer — so these bytes are refused at the dCBOR layer, before the entity layer sees them.

cases.name: scalar_range_missing_endpoint
cases.reason: A datetime range with a from and no to. Both endpoints are required.

cases.name: scalar_range_with_a_unit
cases.reason: A datetime range carrying a unit. The two shapes of scalar-value are exclusive: a range is not a quantity.

cases.name: timestamp_plain_date
cases.reason: Rule 1 (form). "2024-02-20" is a date, and there are no plain dates in Dialog: a day is the range from 00:00:00Z to 23:59:59Z.

cases.name: timestamp_numeric_offset
cases.reason: Rule 2 (UTC only). The offset +00:00 denotes the same instant as Z and MUST NOT be used; a second spelling would be a second digest for one statement.

cases.name: timestamp_lowercase_separator
cases.reason: Rule 3 (uppercase). The date-time separator is a lowercase t, which RFC 3339 permits and Dialog does not.

cases.name: timestamp_lowercase_designator
cases.reason: Rule 3 (uppercase), in the to endpoint: the offset designator is a lowercase z.

cases.name: timestamp_fractional_seconds
cases.reason: Rule 4 (second precision). A fractional-second part MUST NOT be present, not even the zero one written here.

cases.name: timestamp_leap_second
cases.reason: Rule 5 (no leap second). The seconds value 60 that RFC 3339 permits is not a Dialog timestamp.

cases.name: timestamp_not_a_real_date
cases.reason: Rule 6 (a real date). February 2024 has 29 days, so 2024-02-30 denotes no instant. A parser that rolls it forward to 1 March mints a digest for a statement no other implementation holds.

cases.name: timestamp_julian_leap_day
cases.reason: Rule 6 (a real date), in the proleptic Gregorian calendar: 1500 is divisible by 100 and not by 400, so 29 February 1500 does not exist, though the Julian calendar then in civil use had it. Its counterpart, 1600-02-29, is the valid scalar_datetime_leap_day case.

cases.name: range_from_after_to
cases.reason: A range running backwards: "from" MUST NOT be later than "to". Timestamps are fixed-width and most-significant-first, so this is a string comparison and needs no date parsing.
